messages:
Ellie: heads-up — we got a customer escalation (ticket #12345) about a big p95/p99 regression hitting their Dedicated pool in us-west-2 around 09:24 UTC. They saw p95 go from ~120ms to ~800ms and p99 spikes to ~3s for text-generation routes. :rotating_light:
Migs: any recent deploys to the autoscaler or pool config?
Sam: not in infra in the last 24h. I pulled prometheus briefly — there was a sharp inbound QPS spike at 09:23 that coincides with the regression. graph: https://prom.redwood.internal/d/abcd123/ingress?orgId=1 (private)
ops-bot: Alert — dedicated-pool-queue-depth-high (pool-id: dp-02usw2) fired at 09:25 UTC. queue depth peaked at 310, attach failures 12.
support-bot: Customer says they ramped from 30->220 concurrent requests in ~45s, client-side retry enabled. They reported many 503s and slow 200s.
Michael: sounds like pool depletion + attach handshake delay. If autoscaler is conservative we can get queueing while new GPUs are provisioning and warmup. Any attach errors in logs?
Sam: ssh'd into control-plane logs, found repeated: 
```
ERROR attach_manager: handshake timeout waiting for worker (pool=dp-02usw2) id=worker-xyz
WARN attach_manager: dropped attach request after retries=3
```
Andrea: i pushed a change last week that reduced pool prewarm target by 15% to reduce wasted capacity during low utilization windows — might be too aggressive for sudden spikes.
Jia: can we repro quickly? I can run a local load run hitting the dedicated endpoint to reproduce queue/backlog. repro plan: 1) reserve a test dp pool, 2) run 250 concurrent requests with a mix of short prompts, 3) observe p95/p99 and attach logs. Example k6 command: 
```bash
k6 run --vus 250 --duration 30s script.js
```
where script.js hits the dedicated host with the same auth token.
Ellie: please run against a staging dp-02 copy, don't hit prod customer pool. Also capture pool state: 
```bash
redwoodctl pool describe dp-02usw2 --region us-west-2
redwoodctl pool-level-metrics --pool dp-02usw2 --since 10m
```
Migs: I looked at autoscaler events — there was a backoff cycle between 09:23:30 and 09:28:00 because of a transient quota error when requesting GPUs from cloud provider. That delayed new node attachments by ~90s. Cloud team reported transient EC2 provisioning throttles in that AZ.
Sam: combining cloud throttles + reduced prewarm config explains the long tail. When new nodes finally came up they needed extra warmup time (model weights, kv cache fill), so first few requests had high latency.
Jia: repro on staging: confirmed. With a 200->250 ramp, queue depth spikes, attach handshake timeouts observed, and p99 jumps. Logs attached (snip): 
```
[09:23:45] attach_req id=abc status=pending
[09:23:46] attach_req id=abc status=handshake
[09:24:20] attach_req id=abc status=timed_out
[09:24:40] worker-attach success, warmup start
[09:25:05] first token served slow (~1.8s)
```
Andrea: immediate mitigation options?
Michael: short-term: 1) manually increase reserved/burst capacity for affected pool to absorb spike (fast, but costs) 2) temporarily relax autoscaler backoff thresholds to retry provisioning quicker 3) enable prewarm override for that pool so new nodes come pre-loaded.
Ellie: can we do 1) and 2) right now? I'll own the customer comms and ask them to throttle retries.
Migs: i've increased burst-reserve on dp-02usw2 by 40% and set a temporary autoscaler backoff multiplier to 0.5 (lower backoff). Monitoring now.
ops-bot: Note: manual capacity bump will take ~60s to reflect.
Sam: applied a prewarm override for the pool (10% extra warm workers) — will roll back after traffic settles.
Jia: after changes, repro on staging shows queue depth peak reduced from 310->80, p95 down to ~180ms, p99 ~700ms. Still not identical to baseline but much better.
Ellie: good. Next steps (post-incident):
- short term (today): keep bumped reserve and lowered backoff for 2h, ask customer to smooth ramp and reduce aggressive client retries.
- medium term (1-2 weeks): revert the recent prewarm reduction, add an automatic safety floor so prewarm won't be reduced below X for dedicated pools with SLA flag.
- long term: add cloud-provider quota-aware autoscaler strategy — if provider throttling detected, fallback to prioritized warm pool in other region or pre-warmed cold-standby nodes.
Andrea: I'll open a PR to add the safety floor and doc the prewarm tradeoffs.
Migs: will follow up with infra/cloud team on the EC2 provisioning throttle and add alerts for provider-level throttles.
Ellie: i'll draft a short incident note for the customer and our internal postmortem. Thanks everyone for quick reacts. :thumbsup:
support-bot: Customer notified via ticket #12345 with summary and suggested client-side throttling.
ops-bot: Monitoring shows p95 returning toward baseline over the last 3m.
Sam: leaving a snippet of commands we used to triage: 
```bash
# pool state
redwoodctl pool describe dp-02usw2 --region us-west-2
# autoscaler events
redwoodctl autoscaler events --pool dp-02usw2 --since 30m | jq .
# grep attach errors
kubectl -n redwood logs deploy/attach-manager | rg "handshake timeout" -n || true
```
Ellie: ok closing thread once postmortem PR and customer note are posted.
